text:
casey: quick follow-up to the rfc: proposing a lightweight binding-probe handshake so Hosted can safely route to Private/Dedicated variants without live runtime calls. sketch and rollout questions below

pri: love the idea. what's the minimal payload we need from the runtime?

casey: minimal: capability list, capability-version, binding_expiry, and a signature or key_id. example stringified payload: 
`capabilities=[streaming,kv,quant-8bit];ver=1;exp=1680000000;kid=ten-id-42;sig=...`

omar: prefer a signed manifest blob instead of ad-hoc kv pairs. easier to version and audit. signature must be tenant-scoped so Hosted can't accept forged manifests.

tess: ops concern: do we expect Hosted to fetch manifests from Private at bind time? many customers block egress.

casey: design options:
- push-bind: Private publishes manifest to controlplane (or customer uploads) at bind time. Hosted routes to an opaque binding id. no runtime fetches.
- live-probe: Hosted probes runtime at route-resolve time. simpler but breaks air-gapped installs and risks latency spikes.

pri: push-bind wins for air-gapped customers. also gives us an audit trail in controlplane.

omar: revocation: if a tenant rotates keys or wants an immediate kill switch, how do we invalidate bindings?

casey: two mechanisms: short TTL for bindings (e.g., 60s) + a revocation stream. controlplane can push a revoke to Hosted via existing config channel. for out-of-band installs, we include a revocation_nonce in manifest and require local runtime to publish nonce bumps to a dedicated endpoint during enrollment.

tess: add ops checklist: key enrollment docs, storage encryption, revoke runbook, firewall notes. ops-bot: noted, creating infra ticket INFRA-3200.

pri: security: who signs manifests? tenant key or Redwood-issued tenant key? both models have tradeoffs. tenant-signed manifests are best for trust but require customer key enrollment flow.

omar: agree. propose hybrid: accept tenant-signed manifests by default, fallback to Redwood-escrowed signing for customers who opt for simpler onboarding. log which signing mode is used in audit.

casey: good. we'll record sign_mode in binding metadata. also include key_id and key_rotation_policy. legal-bot: flag for data residency implications.

legal-bot: any key material or manifests stored must respect tenant data residency and retention. ensure manifests are treated as customer data and encrypted with tenant-scoped KMS keys where required.

pri: rollout plan idea:
1) dry-run: generate binding recommendations and telemetry only, no routing changes
2) tenant opt-in via console (feature toggle per-tenant)
3) small canary (10 tenants) with ops monitoring
4) wider roll with opt-out for sensitive tenants

omar: tests: synthetic for cold-bind path, measure added p50/p95/p99 on short requests; chaos test for mid-flight revokes; air-gap e2e using signed-manifest download flow.

tess: console UX: show binding state, last-validated time, signer, and reason codes (cap-mismatch, auth, expired). also a link to rebind or request key enrollment.

pri: metrics to emit: binding_success_rate, binding_age_seconds, binding_revocations, binding_fallthroughs (number of requests routed to hosted due to missing or mismatched binding). surface these in the routing dashboard.

omar: admin controls: org-level kill-switch and tenant-level opt-in. require ops approval before enabling auto-apply for auth-sensitive capabilities (kms-mode, egress changes).

casey: compatibility concerns: some runtimes can't represent all canonical capabilities (eg per-minute quotas vs per-second). adapter should emit a mapping delta and we require tenant opt-in when semantics change. default is graceful downgrade + warning.

pri: telemetry should include translation_delta hashed or id'ed so we can link to the adapter version that produced it. helps debugging when adapter logic evolves.

ops-bot: runbook checklist: preflight key enrollment, manifest factory script, firewall/egress docs, revoke commands, metric dashboards to watch, rollback steps. creating RUNBOOK-2201.

legal-bot: include contract language around fallback semantics in Private SLAs. document expected behavior when binding is stale or revoked.

omar: implementation note: controlplane should store binding blobs immutably (append-only) to preserve audit trail and allow rollbacks.

casey: ok i'll draft the manifest-v1 spec (fields, signature scheme, revocation_nonce, expiry), the push-bind API, and the dry-run telemetry hooks. will post link to PR. tagging @pri @tess for review. :rocket:

pri: thanks, ping me when draft is up

tess: i'll coordinate ops preflight once PR lands

ops-bot: created follow-up infra ticket INFRA-3200 and runbook RUNBOOK-2201 from this thread

casey: closing thread - will follow up with PR and timeline. thanks all
